strings.name: Mary Barra
strings.role: General Motors leader · Engineering and manufacturing management
strings.summary: Mary Barra rose from a GM co-op student to engineering and product leadership, becoming the first woman to lead a major global automaker in 2014. She advanced electrification, software and manufacturing changes while confronting ignition-switch recalls, labor relations and autonomous-driving investment challenges. Her career connects technology, capital allocation and safety responsibilities in a transforming industry.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach May 2026. GM's August 2026 activity record corroborates her living status and role. Corporate investment and strategy involve teams, not her contribution alone.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Breaking a leadership barrier
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Became GM CEO in 2014 and chair in 2016, establishing international influence as a woman leading the automotive industry.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Managing an automaker's transformation
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Led GM's electrification and software strategy and changed the direction of Cruise investment in 2024.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: GM reports skilled-trades investment
strings.timeline.event-01.text: During her leadership, GM disclosed nearly $200 million invested over the previous year in US skilled-trades training and careers.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Changes Cruise's autonomy strategy
strings.timeline.event-02.text: GM announced it would stop funding Cruise robotaxi development and focus on assisted and autonomous personal vehicles.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Becomes GM chair
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The board elected her chair, combining the position with her CEO responsibilities.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Testifies on vehicle recalls
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Faced congressional questioning over delayed recalls and vehicle defects, apologizing to affected victims and families.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes GM CEO
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Moved from product leadership to CEO, becoming the first woman to lead a major global automaker.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Leads global product development
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Became senior vice president for global product development, overseeing vehicle design and development work.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Receives a Stanford MBA
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Completed a GM-funded business degree, linking engineering experience with management.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Earns an electrical engineering degree
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Graduated from General Motors Institute, later renamed Kettering University.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Joins GM as a co-op student
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Started at Pontiac, combining education and workplace experience in a long automotive career.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Michigan
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Michigan and raised in a family closely connected to the automotive industry.
strings.influence.rationale: Became GM's first woman CEO and led product development and electrification at a major global manufacturer.
